sentences.english_text: The trainer walked over to a hoop in the middle of the stage.
It was a large, round circle, and the edges of it were lined with paper.
As Drippy watched, the trainer poured gasoline on the paper all around the hoop, then took out a match and lit it so that the hoop was now flaming.
I wonder why he's doing that.
I want to get on with the act.
And suddenly, with a sinking feeling, Drippy realized that this was the act.
The little white poodle started racing toward the flaming hoop.
He's not going to jump through that.
He can't. Not with me on him.
And at that instant, the poodle reached the hoop, leaped into the air, and jumped right through the flames.
I'm going to melt, exclaimed Drippy as the heat of the flames reached him.
But a second later, they were safely through.
And the audience went wild with excitement.
They cheered and applauded and stamped their feet, and the poodle moved to the center of the stage to take a bow.
You're wonderful, someone from the audience called out.
Thank you.
Thank you very much.
Oh, it's so good to be a star and have everybody love you.
I think I'm going to make show business my life.
I'm a natural talent.
Wait until I tell my mother and my father and my sisters and brothers and cousins how I starred in a stage show and how the audience cheered me.
Everybody's going to be so jealous.
As the dog trotted off stage with a trainer, Drippy slid off Prince's neck.
He wanted to stay and see the rest of the show.
